entries.english: Tell him to make haste
entries.translation: Wachne oret piyo
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Put the water on the fire

entries.pronunciation: ket pi e kendo. mur pi

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: There is no oil in it

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Lay the table

entries.english: The water is not boiling

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Boil some eggs
entries.translation: Tedi tong'gwen moko
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: The meat is tough. It is not cooked enough

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Take away the plates
entries.translation: Gol sende
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Ring the bell
entries.translation: Go okot
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: At what time do you have your meals?

entries.english: A little coffee when I get up
entries.translation: Adwaro kahawa matin k'achiew

entries.english: Breakfast is at eight o'clock

entries.english: Go and buy in the market
entries.translation: Dhi ng'iew e chiro
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Get me some fish
entries.translation: Dhi omna rech
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: What sort of meat is to be had?
entries.translation: Ring'o manade mantiye e chiro?

entries.english: There is beef every day
entries.translation: Ring dhiang' emabetiye pilepile
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Sometimes mutton and goat

entries.pronunciation: ndalo moko ring rombo gi diel nitiye
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: There is plenty of fowl
entries.translation: Gwen nitiye mang'eny
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Are there any vegetables?

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Make my bed properly
entries.translation: Pedhina kitandana maber
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Sweep my room every morning
entries.translation: Ywe oda okinyi ka okinyi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Put my boots in the sun and clean them well
entries.translation: Ket wuochena e chieng' kendo iywegi maber
entries.pronunciation: ket wuochena e chieng' kendo iywegi maber
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Close the door. Open the window
entries.translation: Chiegi dhoot. Yaw dirisa
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Give me the keys
entries.translation: Mia funguo
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Wash these clothes. Count the clothes

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Use plenty of soap. Spread them in the sun
entries.translation: Ti gi sabun mang'eny. Moygi e chieng'
entries.pronunciation: ti gi sabun mang'eny. moygi e chieng
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Have you washed yourself?
entries.translation: Iselwokori?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do not be afraid. I come to visit the people
entries.translation: Kik iluor. Abiro neno jo dalani
entries.pronunciation: kik iluor. abiro neno jo dalani
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Call him out. Tell him I want to see him
entries.translation: Dhi luonge, obi. Wachne adwaro nene
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Is it an important village?
entries.translation: Dalani ng'ongo?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: How many people? / How many houses?
entries.translation: Jo dalani gin adi? / Udi gin adi?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Have you a good number of cattle?
entries.translation: In gi dhok mang'eny?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Are the people quiet?
entries.translation: Pacho okwe?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: May I get something to drink?

entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: This is not clear water
entries.translation: Pi oduore, oklew
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do you get the water from the river?
entries.translation: Iumbo pi aora?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: What sort of food do you eat?
entries.translation: Ichamo chiemo manade?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Plenty of sweet potatoes
entries.translation: Rabuon emachamo mang'eny
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do they also plant sesamum and groundnuts?
entries.translation: Bende gipidhi nyim gi njugu?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Are there any beans? And meal and Indian corn?
entries.translation: Oganda nitiye? Gi mogo gi banda?
entries.pronunciation: oganda nitiye? gi mogo gi banda
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Is the sugar-cane very sweet?
entries.translation: Niyang' mit ahinya?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Where do you get the honey?
entries.translation: Mor kich inwang'o kanye?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Is there anybody sick? What is the matter with him?
entries.translation: Nitiye ng'ato matuwo? Otuwo ang'o?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: I have pains all over my body
entries.translation: Ringra duto rama
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: I cannot take any food
entries.translation: Chiemo duto tinde otama
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: I have fever. / I have diarrhoea. / I have dysentery
entries.translation: Midusi maka. / Adiewo. / Adiewo remo
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: I cannot sleep during the night
entries.translation: Nindo otama otieno
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Show me your tongue. Open your mouth
entries.translation: Nyisa lewi. Ng'am dhogi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Take this medicine twice a day. Swallow it with water
entries.translation: Madh yadhni diriyo chieng' achiel. Mwony gi pi
entries.pronunciation: madh yadhni diriyo chieng' achiel. mwony gi pi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: If you want anything, tell me
entries.translation: K'idwaro gimoro, wachina
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Put on this ointment. Tie it up with this bandage
entries.translation: Wiriye yadhini. Itwe gi nangani
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do not stretch your arm for six days
entries.translation: Kik irie badi ndalo auchiel
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: I shall come again. He is much better to-day
entries.translation: Naduogi kendo. Kawono ohingo nyoro
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: What is your name? Where do you come from?
entries.translation: Nyingi ng'a? In jakanye?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Do you understand cultivation?
entries.translation: Ing'eyo pur?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Are you a strong man?
entries.translation: In ng'ato matek?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Come quick. Go on, work hard
entries.translation: Bi piyo. Tiuru piyo
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: You can rest a little in the middle of the day
entries.translation: Unyalo yweyo matin odiechieng'
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Come along to the garden
entries.translation: Ero, bi, wadhi puodho
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Take a hoe. Dig from here to there
entries.translation: Maki kwer. Pur nyaka a kaeni nyaka chopi kacha
entries.pronunciation: maki kwer. pur nyaka a kaeni nyaka chopi kacha
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Put the grass aside
entries.translation: Ket lum tenge
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Take the potatoes to the garden
entries.translation: Ter rabuon e puodho
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: This man works well
entries.translation: Ng'atni otiyo maber
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Go and plant there
entries.translation: Dhi pidhi kacha
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Take out (dig up) the potatoes. Take care not to cut them
entries.translation: Kuny rabuon. Kuny mos, kik ipudhigi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Put them in these bags
entries.translation: Rwakigi e kiropegi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Make haste, it will rain. Send it home before the rain
entries.translation: Reti, wang' koth nochwe. Ter dala ka koth podi
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Leave the work now. Go home altogether
entries.translation: Weuru tich koro. Dhiuru dala uduto
entries.pronunciation: weuru tich koro. dhiuru dala uduto
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: You will be paid to-morrow
entries.translation: Kiny nunwang' musachu
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: We shall start to-morrow
entries.translation: Kiny wanadhi safar
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Have you all the loads ready?
entries.translation: Isetweyo gikmoko duto?
entries.context: Mill-Hill Fathers (1920–1921) A Handbook of the Kavirondo Language (Phraseology pp. 102–117) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus Dholuo (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: Your skin is your largest organ, and it's important to take care of it both inside and out. Here are some tips for healthy skin:

entries.english: * Drink plenty of water: Water is essential for healthy skin, as it helps to keep your skin hydrated and soft. Aim to drink eight glasses of water per day.

entries.english: * Eat a healthy diet: Eating a healthy diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can help to improve your skin's appearance.

entries.english: * Get regular exercise: Exercise can help to improve your circulation and promote healthy skin. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week.
entries.translation: *Timo orako mapile: Orako nyalo konyo bero ringo mar remo kod rito pien del maber. Tem itim orako mamor mor-ma iye tek kuom dakika mok tin ne 30 kuom ndalo mathoth e juma.

entries.english: * Get enough sleep: When you don't get enough sleep, your body produces more of the stress hormone cortisol, which can lead to inflammation and skin problems. Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per night.

entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * Protect your skin from the sun: The sun's UV rays can damage your skin and lead to premature aging, wrinkles, and skin cancer.

entries.english: But in 1974, a military junta known as the Derg seized power and began a brutal campaign of repression.
entries.translation: To e higa mar 1974, grup mar jolweny maloko loch mong'ere kaka Derg noloko loch kendo chako kampen mar thiro ji githuon.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The Derg's policies led to widespread famine and poverty, and millions of Ethiopians were forced to flee their homes.
entries.translation: Chenro mag Derg nomiyo kech kod dhier ogoyo tach, kendo jo Ethiopia tara gi gana nochuno oringo owuok e delni gi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 1991, a coalition of rebel groups known as the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) overthrew the Derg.
entries.translation: E higa mar 1991, riwruok mar jok ma obala mong'ere kaka Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) ne oloko loch mar Derg.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The EPRDF established a new government and promised to restore peace and prosperity to Ethiopia.
entries.translation: Jo EPRDF go noloso sirkal manyien kendo singore mar duogo kue kod dongruok e Ethiopia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, the EPRDF's rule has been plagued by human rights abuses, corruption, and political repression.
entries.translation: Kata kamano, loch mar EPRDF opong' kod keth mar ratich dhano, mibadhi, kod thiro ji kisiasa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: In 2018, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed took office and pledged to reform the country.
entries.translation: E higa mar 2018, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed ne okao apis kendo singo mar loko pinyno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He released political prisoners, lifted restrictions on the media, and began peace talks with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the former ruling party of Tigray.
entries.translation: Ne ogonyo josiasa mane otue, wito oko obadho mane oket ne ute fwambo kod keyo, kendo chako twak mag loso kue kod duond bura mar Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), mane en chama mane niye loch e gwenge mag Tigray.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, the peace talks broke down in June 2020, and the TPLF launched an offensive against the Ethiopian military.
entries.translation: Kata kamano, twak mag loso kue nokethore e dwe mar auchiel 2020, kendo jokanyo mag TPLF nomoko lweny kod jolweny mag piny owacho ma Ethiopia.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The ensuing conflict has been devastating.
entries.translation: Lwenyno osekelo midhiero mathoth.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The fighting has displaced millions of people, and the humanitarian situation is dire.
entries.translation: Lwenyno osedaro ji tara gi gana, kendo kwan jok madwaro kony osedhi malo ahinya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s coming from the kitchen, so I get up to investigate.
entries.translation: Owuok e jikon, koro aa malo mondo anon ane.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I creep down the hallway, careful not to make a sound.
entries.translation: Alidho mos ka atemo mondo kik winja.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The clacking is getting louder.
entries.translation: Kokono medore.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I peer around the corner into the kitchen and see Mum standing at the sink, staring out the window.
entries.translation: Agoyo wanga e kona ka arango jikon kendo aneno mama ka ochung' but kama iluoke sende, ka orango oko e dirisa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She looks pale and shaken. “Mum?” I ask.
entries.translation: Oneno ma ojony kendo oluor. "Mama?" apenjo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She doesn’t turn around.
entries.translation: Ok olokore.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “Mum, what’s wrong?” She takes a deep breath and turns to face me.
entries.translation: "Mama, ang'o ma rach?" Ogamo yweyo matut kae olokore kochima.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Her eyes are wide and filled with fear.
entries.translation: Omoro wengene kendo wengene opong kod luoro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “There’s something outside,” she says. “Something big.”
entries.translation: "Nitiere gimoro kok," owacho. "Gima duong'."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I follow her gaze out the window.
entries.translation: Arango kuma orango oko mar dirisa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: At first, I don’t see anything.
entries.translation: Mokuongo', ok ane gimoro amora.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But then, I notice a movement in the shadows.
entries.translation: Bange, aneno tipo mar gimoro mabiro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s a large, dark shape, and it’s moving towards the house.
entries.translation: Oduong', orateng' kendo obiro kochomo ot.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “What is it?” I ask. “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But I don’t think it’s friendly.”
entries.translation: "En ang'o?" apenjo. "Akia," Mama owacho. "To ok apar ni en gima ber."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The creature gets closer.
entries.translation: Gino medo biro machiegni.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s tall and slender, with long, spindly legs.
entries.translation: Orabora kendo odhero, en kod tielo mabocho to ohero.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Its body is covered in black fur, and its head is a smooth, round ball.
entries.translation: Yier marateng' oumo dende, kendo wiye chalo opira ma yom to oluorore.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It has no eyes, but I can see two large, pointed ears.
entries.translation: Oonge kod wang, to anyalo neno it ariyo madongo to ochikore.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “What are we going to do?” I ask.
entries.translation: "Wadhi timo ang'o?" apenjo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “We need to get out of here,” Mum says. “Now.”
entries.translation: "Onego wawuog ka," Mama owacho. "Sani."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We run out of the kitchen and into the living room.
entries.translation: Wawuok oko mar jikon kod ng'wech wadonjo e rum mar yweyo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “Mum! Dad!” I cry. “There’s something outside!”
entries.translation: "Mama! Baba!" Aywak. "Nitiere gimoro oko!"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad looks up from the TV. “What is it?” he asks.
entries.translation: Baba tingo wange wuok e TV. "En ang'o?" openjo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But it’s big and it’s coming this way.”
entries.translation: "Akia," Mama wacho. "To oduong' kendo ochomo ka."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad gets up from the couch.
entries.translation: Baba chung' wuok e kom.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: “We need to get out of here,” he says.
entries.translation: "Onego wawuog ka," owacho.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We all run for the front door.
entries.translation: Wate waringo ka wachomo dhot ma mbele.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Mum unlocks it and we rush outside.
entries.translation: Mama yawe kendo wate wahau oko.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The creature is right behind us.
entries.translation: Gino nitere e tokwa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It’s so close I can feel its hot breath on the back of my neck.
entries.translation: Ochiegni kodwa anyalo winjo muya maliet ma ogolo e tok nguta.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We run to the car and get in.
entries.translation: Waringo kawachomo nyamburko kae wadonjo e iye.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Dad starts the engine and we peel out of the driveway.
entries.translation: Baba moko nyamburko kendo wawuok e yor nyamburko.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The creature chases after us, but we’re too fast.
entries.translation: Gino laowa, to kata kamano wadhi piyo ahinya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Movies have long been a powerful force in shaping our culture and our values.
entries.translation: Sinema kuom ndalo mang'eny osebedo gima nigi teko mathoth kuom yor dak kod gik ma wamiyo pek.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They can influence our beliefs about everything from love and romance to war and violence.
entries.translation: Ginyalo loko kaka waneno gik moko te kochakore e hera kod timo timbe hera nyaka lweny kod dhao.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And they have a particularly strong influence on our ideas about gender roles.
entries.translation: Kendo gin kod teko mathoth ewi kaka waneno gik tije monego kaluwore kod chuech mar ngato.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For decades, Hollywood has perpetuated the stereotype of the ideal wife as a beautiful, submissive, and domestic woman who puts her husband and children first.
entries.translation: Kuom higni mathoth, kambi mar Hollywood osetemo ahinya temo nyiso ni dhako maber en dhako ma jaber, oluoro chuore, kendo bet e dhot to oketo chuore kod nyithinde mbele.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This image is often reinforced by the way that female characters are portrayed in movies.
entries.translation: Picha ni itemo sir ahinya kaluwore kaka josinema mamon itango e sinema.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For example, a study by the Geena Davis Institute found that in the top 100 films of 2017, only 30% of female characters had speaking roles, and only 12% of those characters were working outside the home.
entries.translation: Kuom ranyisi, nonro mane otim kod Greena Davis Institute noyudo ni e sinembe 100 mane nimalo e higa mar 2017, atamalo 30 kende emane nigi duol, kendo mana atamalo 12 kende kuomgi ema tiyo oko mar dala.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The majority of female characters were portrayed as either romantic interests or mothers.
entries.translation: Ng'eny mag josinema mamon ne inyiso kaka joma ohero timo timbe mag hera kata kaka mine.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This narrow representation of women in film sends a powerful message to viewers about what it means to be a woman.
entries.translation: Yo madiny mar nyiso mine e sinembe oro ote motegno ne joneno ewi gima bedo miyo en.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It suggests that women's primary role is to be attractive and nurturing, and that their success is measured by their relationships with men and children.
entries.translation: Otemo nyiso ni tij joma miyo maduong' en bedo majaber kod rito nyithindo, kendo ni dhi maber e ngima gi ipimo kod tudruok e kindgi kod chuo gi nyithindo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: This idealized image of the wife can be harmful to women in several ways.
entries.translation: Pichani molosi mar dhako nyalo kelo midhiero ne joma miyo e yore mang'eny.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Doctor, I've been having this terrible stomach pain for the past few days.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Laktar, asebedo kod ich maremo malichni kuom ndalo mathin mokalo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's so bad that I can't eat or sleep.
entries.translation: Orach ma ok anyal chiemo kata nindo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It's a sharp, stabbing pain that comes and goes.
entries.translation: En rem machucho mabich kendo oja biro kae olal.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Can you tell me more about the pain? Where is it located?
entries.translation: Laktar: Be inyalo nyiso mathoth ewi rem ni? Iwinje gi kar kanye?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: It's mostly in my lower abdomen, right around my belly button, but it sometimes radiates to my back.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Ng'enyne awinje e piny iya korka achwich e aluora mar penda, to seche moko oringo nyaka e ng'eya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Does anything make the pain worse?
entries.translation: Laktra: Be nitie gima miyo rem medo bedo marach moloyo?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Eating seems to make it worse, especially fatty or greasy foods.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Chamo chiemo chal gima miyo omedo bedo marach ahinya, ahinya to chiemo motimo mo mathoth.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: And does anything make it better.?
entries.translation: Laktar: To be nitiere gima miyo bet odok chien?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Lying down seems to help a little.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Nindo piny chal gima miyo odok piny matin.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Does the pain come and go, or is it constant?
entries.translation: Laktar: Remno biro to lal, koso en gima osiko?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: It's constant. It's just a dull ache, but it's really uncomfortable.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Osiko, En aena rem mapile, to omiyo ok awinj maber.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: Have you had any other symptoms? Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea?
entries.translation: Laktar: Be in kod ranyisi mamoko? Ting'ruok mar chuny, ng'ok, dieo?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: No, just the pain.
entries.translation: Jatuo: Ooyo, mana rem.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: I see. Well, it sounds like you're having a case of gastritis.
entries.translation: Laktar: Aneno. Chal gima in kod tuo mar gastritis.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining.
entries.translation: Gastritis en kuot mar i matumbo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It can be caused by a number of things, including eating spicy or fatty foods, drinking alcohol, or taking certain medications.
entries.translation: Inyalo kele kod gik mathoth, moting'o koda chamo chiemo moted kod kid mamedo ndhadho kata chiemo motimo mo mathoth, madho kong'o, kata tiyo kod yedhe moko.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Patient: Is it serious?
entries.translation: Jatuo: Be en tuo malich ahinya?
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Doctor: It can be, but in most cases it's not.
entries.translation: Laktar: Onyalo bedo malich ahinya, to thothne ok en.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I'm going to prescribe you some medication to help relieve the pain and inflammation.
entries.translation: Adhi ndikoni yedhe mabiro konyo duoko piny rem kod kuot.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: You should also avoid eating spicy or fatty foods, and drink plenty of fluids.
entries.translation: Bende onego iwe chamo chiemo ma oted kod gik mamedo ndadho kata chiemo motimo mo mathoth, kendo imodh mathoth.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Ingredients:
entries.translation: Gik mantie:
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.translation: *Mogo mitiyo godo e loso gik moko te okombe 1

entries.translation: *Mogo mar almond okombe 1
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: * 1/2 cup granulated sugar
entries.translation: *Sukari ma rachar nus okombe
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.translation: *Sukari ma rabuor akuota mar okombe

entries.english: Instructions:
entries.translation: Okang' miluwo:
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour an 8-inch round cake pan.
entries.translation: 1. Chwak oven ma temperecha chop 350 digris F (175 digris C). Wir mo kod mogo inji 8 e pier pan mar cake.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flours, granulated sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
entries.translation: 2. Ol kae irud kaachiel moke go, sukari ma rachar, sukari ma rabuor, beking poda, beking soda, kod chumbi e bakul maniye diere.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 3. In a large bowl, cream together the butter and egg until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
entries.translation: 3. Ei bakul maduong', rud mor agwela cha kod tong' ma obedo mayom kendo yot. Chwad nyai tong' cha kod mor almond cha.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk. Mix until just combined.
entries.translation: 4. Mos mos med gik motuo go ei gik mang'ich ka iriwo gi matin matin kod chak. Rud ma gi riwre.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: 5. Fold in the almond flour until evenly distributed.
entries.translation: 5. Med mok almond irud ma opogre marom.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It was a hot summer day in July when I finally turned 16 years old.
entries.translation: Ne en odiechieng' maliet e dwe mar abiriyo kane arwako higa mar 16.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I had been eagerly anticipating this day for as long as I could remember, and now that it was finally here, I couldn't wait to get started on my road to freedom.
entries.translation: Ne arito gi sirimo odiechieng'ni kuom ndalo mathoth tek ni ne anyalo paro, to koro kane osechopo, ne ok anyal rito chako wuodha mar yudo uhuru.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The first step was to take the written test.
entries.translation: Ondamo mokuongo ne timo penj mondiki.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I studied hard for weeks, and I was confident that I would pass.
entries.translation: Ne asomo matek kuom jumbe, kendo ne an kod chir ni adhi kalo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: On the day of the test, I arrived at the DMV early and took my seat in the waiting room.
entries.translation: E odiechieng' mar penj, ne achopo momondo DMV kendo kao kom e rum mar rito.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: After a few hours, my name was called, and I was ushered into a small room with a computer.
entries.translation: Bang' seche matin, nyinga nene oluongi, kendo orwaka e rum moro matin manitie e kompyuta.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The test was surprisingly easy, and I finished it in no time.
entries.translation: Penj no ne yot miwuoro, kendo ne atieke piyo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: A few days later, I received a letter in the mail informing me that I had passed the written test.
entries.translation: Bang' ndalo machuok, ne ayudo oboke ei email mara manyisa ni ne akalo penj mindiko no.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The next step was to schedule a driving test.
entries.translation: Ondamo maluwe ne en pango penj mar riembo gare.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I called the DMV and made an appointment for the following week.
entries.translation: Ne agocho ne DMV kendo yudo apointment kodgi juma maluwe.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The day of my driving test arrived, and I was more nervous than I had ever been in my life.
entries.translation: Odiechieng' mar penj mara mar riembo ne ochopo, kendo ne abedo gi luoro mang'eny moloyo seche duto e ngima na.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: I drove to the DMV with my mom, who would be accompanying me on the test.
entries.translation: Ne ariembo nyaka DMV kod mamana, ma be ne dhi koda e penj mara no.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Heartbreak," sighed the poet, "is the cruelest of afflictions.
entries.translation: "Chuny monyosore," jandiko no ne ong'ur, "en e chandruok ma kwiny ahinya mogik.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a pain that pierces the soul and leaves us feeling empty and alone.
entries.translation: En lit machuoyo chuny kendo weyo ka wawinjo ni wadong' nono kendo waongee gimoro.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a fire that burns from within, consuming us with its flames.
entries.translation: En mach ma wang'o wa kowuok e iwa, kendo ochamowa gi liel ma oliel go no.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: It is a storm that tears us apart, leaving us broken and scarred.
entries.translation: En yamo maduong' ma yechowa pogowa, owewa ka watur kendo waluor.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: But even in the midst of our heartbreak, there is hope.
entries.translation: Makmana ni kata e dier chuny monyosre ma wan go no, nitie geno.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For even as our hearts are broken, they are also made new.
entries.translation: To kata ka chunje wa otur, bende itimo chunjewa go bedo manyien.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We are given the opportunity to learn from our mistakes and to grow stronger.
entries.translation: Omiwa thuolo mar puonjre kowuok kuom ketho magwa kendo mondo wadong ka wabedo motegno ahinya.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: We are given the chance to find love again, even if it is different than the love we have lost.
entries.translation: Omiwa thuolo mar yudo hera kendo, kata ka opogre gi hera ma waselalo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: So let us not despair in our heartbreak.
entries.translation: Omiyo chunywa kik jog kaluwore kod chunywa mool.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Let us instead embrace it as a part of life.
entries.translation: To makmana ni warwake kaka gino matimre e ngima.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Let us learn from it and grow from it.
entries.translation: We wayud puonj kowuok kuome kendo wadongre kode.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: And let us never give up on the hope of finding love again"
entries.translation: To kik wating' badwa ne geno mar yudo hera kendo no"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Judaism and Kosher Kosher is a set of dietary laws in Judaism.
entries.translation: Yore mag Jo-Yahudi kod Kosher Kosher en kanyakla maduong' mar chike mag chiemo e yore mag Jo-Yahudi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These laws define which foods are permissible to eat and which are not.
entries.translation: Chike gi lero ni chiemo mage ma oyie ni ng'ato mondo ochak to mage ma ok oyiene ng'ato chamo.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher foods are those that are considered to be fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
entries.translation: Chiemo mag Kosher gin chiemo ma okaw kaka chiemo maber ka ichamo kaluwore gi chike mag Jo-Yahudi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The laws of kosher are based on the Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.
entries.translation: Chike mag Kosher luwore kod Torah, andike abich mokuongo e Muma mar Jo-Hibrania.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: These laws prohibit the consumption of certain animals, such as pigs and shellfish, as well as the consumption of blood and meat from animals that have not been slaughtered in a specific way.
entries.translation: Chike gi okumo chamo lee mamoko, kaka anguro kod rach mantie gi kode, kaachiel gi chamo remo kod ring'o mar lee ma ok oyang' e yoo madwarore.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher foods are also subject to a number of other regulations, such as the separation of dairy and meat products.
entries.translation: Chiemb Kosher bende luwo chike mamoko mang'eny, kaka pogo gigo mag chak gi mak ring'o.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Kosher food is prepared in a way that ensures that it is fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
entries.translation: Chiemb Kosher iloso e yoo maneno ni ober ka ichame kaluwore kod chike mag Jo-Yahudi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The observance of kosher laws is an important part of Jewish religious practice.
entries.translation: Luwo chike mag Kosher en okang' maduong' e timbe mag tin mar Jo-Yahudi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: For many Jews, eating kosher food is a way to show their devotion to God and to connect with their heritage.
entries.translation: Ne Jo-Yahudi mang'eny, chamo chiemb kosher en yoo mar nyiso chiwruok margi ne Nyasaye kod riwruok gi gikeni mag gi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: There are a number of reasons why Jews observe kosher laws.
entries.translation: Nitie gik mang'eny ma oiyo Jo-Yahudi luwo ga chike mag kosher.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Some of these reasons are based on religious beliefs, while others are based on practical considerations Religious reasons Jews believe that God gave the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai.
entries.translation: Moko kuom weche go lure gi yie margi mar din, to moko luwore kod gigo ma giluwo ka Jo-Yahudi go nigi yie ni Nyasaye ne omiyo Musa Torah no e Got Sinai.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "I'm telling you, this is going to be the funniest thing ever," said Tom.
entries.translation: "Anyisi, mae dhibedo gimamiyo ji nyiero malich ahinya mapok ne odwar oyud," Tom ne owacho.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Just wait until you see the look on people's faces when they see my new tattoo!"
entries.translation: "Rit arita ine kaka ji dhi neno ka gineno gima agoro manyien e denda!"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "I don't know, Tom," said his friend, Ben.
entries.translation: "Akia, Tom," Ben ma osiepne nowacho.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "A green question mark on your forehead seems like it could be a bit of a risky move."
entries.translation: "Alama mar penjo ma majan mantie e pat wiyi neno ni onyalo bedo ondambo ma ket nyalo kelo masira."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "That's what makes it so funny," said Tom "People are going to be so confused.
entries.translation: "Mano e gima timo onyalo miyo ji nyiero," Tom ne owacho "Ji dhibedo gi paro mochochni.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They'll be asking themselves all sorts of questions, like 'What does it mean?' or 'Why did he do that?'"
entries.translation: Gibiro penjre penjo duto tee madi gipenj, kaka 'Mano tiende en ang'o?' kata 'Ang'o ma omiyo ne otimo mano?'"
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Or they'll just think you're an idiot," said Ben.
entries.translation: "Kata gibiro mana paro ni ifuwo," Ben ne owacho.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: "Nah, they'll get it," said Tom. "Trust me."
entries.translation: "Dawe, gibiro ng'eyo tiende," Tom ne owacho. "Yie kuom gima anyisi."
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: So Tom got the tattoo, and sure enough, people were confused.
entries.translation: Omiyo Tom ne ogoro gima ne odwaro goro e dende, to adier, ji ne obedo gi paro mochochni.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They asked him all sorts of questions, and he loved every minute of it.
entries.translation: Ne gipenje penjo mopogre opogre duto tee mane digipenj, to ne ohero okang' ka okang' mar penjo go.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: He even started a blog about his tattoo, where he would post pictures and answer questions from his readers.
entries.translation: Ne ochako nyaka ndiko weche ma otudre gi piche mogor e del, kama ne onyalo goyee piche kod duoko penjo mag josomo masomo gik mondiko.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Indira Gandhi was the first and only woman to serve as Prime Minister of India.
entries.translation: Indira Gandhi ne en miyo mokuongo kendo makende mane otiyo kaka Jatend Piny India.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was born in 1917 into a prominent political family, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Prime Minister of India.
entries.translation: Ne onyuole e higa mar 1917 e anyuola mane ong'ere ahinya e weche siasa, to wuon gi, Jawaharlal Nehru, ema ne en jatelo mokuongo mar piny India.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Indira Gandhi was educated in India and England, and she married Feroze Gandhi in 1942.
entries.translation: Indira Gandhi ne osomo e piny India kod Uingeresa, to Feroze Gandhi ne okende e higa mar 1942.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: They had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay.
entries.translation: Ne gin gi nyithindo ariyo ma yawuoyi, ma gin Rajiv kod Sanjay.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gandhi began her political career in 1955, when she was elected to the Indian Parliament.
entries.translation: Gandhi ne ochako siasa mare e higa mar 1955, kane oyiere e Od Bura mar India.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She served in various ministerial positions in the government of her father, and in 1966 she became Prime Minister after his death.
entries.translation: Ne otiyo e migepe mopogre opogre e piny owacho mar wuon gi, to e higa mar 1966 ne obedo Jatend pinyno bang' tho mar wuon gi.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gandhi was a controversial figure, and her policies were often criticized.
entries.translation: Gandhi ne en jatelo ma yore ne kelo ywarruok, kendo chike mage ne ipingo kinde ka kinde.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was accused of being authoritarian and of suppressing dissent.
entries.translation: Ne ikwede ni ne otiyo kod agoko kendo ne othiro joma obalo kode.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: However, she was also a popular leader, and she is credited with modernizing India and improving the lives of its people.
entries.translation: Kata kamano, ne en jatelo bende mane ong'ere ahinya, kendo imiye puoch mar timo piny India obedo manya sani kod bero ngima mar jo india.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.
entries.translation: Jorit mag Sikh ne onego Gandhi e higa mar 1984 nikech weche siasa.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: She was succeeded by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.
entries.translation: Wuode ma iluongo ni Rajiv Gandhi ema ne okao kare.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: Gandhi's life and career were marked by many challenges, but she never gave up on her dream of a better India.
entries.translation: Ngima mar Gandhi kaachiel kod tije ne oyudo ng'ikruok mang'eny, to ne ok oting'o bade e lek mare mar loso piny India.
entries.context: Google Research SMOLDoc Parallel Corpus (smoldoc__en_luo, CC-BY-4.0, https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/smol)

entries.english: The term is frequently used interchangeably with the term climate change, though the latter refers to both human- and naturally produced warming and the effects it has on our planet.
entries.translation: Medruok mar liet e piny kinde ka kinde itiyo gago kaachiel gi lokruok mar kit yamo, mak mana ni lokruok mar kit yamo itiyo ga go e nyiso liet ma ikelo gi dhano kod yo mapile kanyakla gi gigo ma otimo e pinywa.

entries.english: Most of the current warming trend is extremely likely (greater than 95 percent probability) the result of human activity since the 1950s and is proceeding at an unprecedented rate over decades to millennia.
